promptHead: Athlete goal: marathon (Wexley Lakes Marathon) on Sun Nov 1 2026, 6 weeks out, target under 3:45.

new.headline: You added 16 miles over the plan and finished a 20-miler on tight calves, so this week pulls volume back a notch and puts marathon pace into the long run. Progress is real, but the jump was too big to repeat.

answers.question: I ran way more than the plan and felt fine. Can I keep this up?
answers.answer: Short answer: no, not at this rate. You went from 37 to 53 miles in one jump while the plan asked for 38, and the load numbers flagged it as overload. The last time life pushed you hard, back in mid-August, the right knee flared on a long run; that is the pattern I want to avoid now that we are inside the final stretch to Nov 1. Keep the appetite, spend it where it counts: the long run and the quality session. Rest days stay rest, and easy days stay easy and under HR 145. We will grow volume, just in smaller steps.

new.analysis:
## Why this week looks like this

The main lesson from last week is that you have the fitness to do more, but your body is not yet adapted to carrying it. Easy pace at 139 bpm is a good signal; the 20-miler at 88 percent zone 3 is a warning that "easy long" slid into "steady long". We will protect the next six weeks by holding easy truly easy.

Volume comes down a little to about 42 miles, which is still well above your pre-build base and keeps the long run meaningful. The long run drops to 16 mi so we can introduce marathon pace cleanly; expect 8:35/mi for the goal of under 3:45. Wednesday is your one quality session, with 5 miles at marathon pace sandwiched by easy miles, which is the key workout of a marathon build.

Mon and Fri are real rest. If you feel springy, spend it on Wednesday's marathon-pace block or on Sunday, not on bonus easy miles. Keep an eye on the calves this week; if they stay tight, back off pace before you back off distance.

safetyCallouts.title: Watch the calves.
safetyCallouts.body: If tightness turns into pain that worsens day to day, or you feel a sharp pull, stop the run and see a physio before pushing on.
